expectations.text: The terrain produces mechanical consequences — cover, movement cost, visibility limits — not just flavor text.
expectations.evidence: Extensive terrain mechanics: tidal current DC 12-14 Athletics, depth progression (waist→chest→neck over rounds), ford stones Acrobatics DC 11, mist obscures 30+ ft (disadvantage on ranged attacks), CON save DC 10 per round for exhaustion, movement speed penalties by depth.

expectations.text: Both factions have named objectives independent of the party, creating a three-way situation.
expectations.evidence: [[Countless]]: deny [[the-passage]] the ford before relief arrives. [[The Passage]]: hold crossing until reinforcements. Party is a complication, not primary target for either.

expectations.text: The party can choose sides, play factions against each other, sneak through, or retreat — at least three viable approaches.
expectations.evidence: Six ways out: sprint across, wade upstream, ally with the-passage, scale rocks to flank countless, swim downstream, or wait for reinforcements.

expectations.text: Opposition section names each faction's goal, method, and what triggers their attention on the party.
expectations.evidence: Col-md blocks for both factions: Intent, Opening move, Behavior, Breaking point, Resources. Countless fires indiscriminately; Passage won't target party unless attacked.

expectations.text: Stakes are concrete: what the party gains or loses by engaging vs avoiding.
expectations.evidence: Resolution table with four outcomes: Objective gained (safe crossing, known to passage), Costly success (lost equipment, water-logged), Withdrawal/defeat (stranded, alternate route), Unexpected solution (political entanglement).

expectations.text: The contest changes the physical situation through one engagement, then hands off to a Development.
expectations.evidence: Line 129: Next Development named. Changed state section describes world after crossing. Single engagement with clear end conditions.
